conventions.convention: G is finite, A is finite abelian and additive, ρ is a left action, and β is a normalized inhomogeneous 3-cocycle. The skeletal associator runs from (gh)k to g(hk) with label β(g,h,k).

Simplices follow the total vertex order; cochain values lie at the first vertex. Transport from j to i is ρ(a_ij), flatness is a_ij a_jk=a_ik, and backgrounds satisfy δ_a B=a*β with alternating signs +,−,+,− on tetrahedra.
Successive vertex gauge labels g then h compose as hg. Raw vertex/edge parameter pairs remain distinct even when their induced maps on backgrounds coincide.
A 2-arrow t has fixed vertex labels g and satisfies λ′−λ=δ_b t. Vertical composition adds cochains; horizontal composition is s+ρ_h t. The associator from ((k∘h)∘g) to k∘(h∘g) is β(k_i,h_i,g_i).
Relative objects restrict exactly to the fixed boundary background; relative arrows have identity vertex labels and zero edge labels on the subcomplex, and relative 2-arrows vanish there.

load_bearing.statement: For finite G, finite abelian A, a left action ρ and normalized 3-cocycle β, a background on a finite ordered simplicial complex is a flat edge cochain a and a face cochain B satisfying δ_a B=a*β. The definition specifies the twisted differential, vertex/edge gauge transformation formulas, and representative change β′=β+δ_ρ c, B′=B+a*c.

For a finite ordered complex, finite G, finite abelian A, a left action ρ, normalized 3-cocycle β, and background (a,B), arbitrary vertex/edge gauge parameters preserve flatness and δ_a B=a*β. Successive transformations have the displayed τ-corrected composite (hg,ν), the displayed reverse induces an inverse, and induced maps on background cochains compose associatively.

Backgrounds are objects; raw gauge parameter pairs are 1-arrows; vertex cochains t with λ′−λ=δ_b t are 2-arrows for fixed g. Composition uses τ, horizontal composition is s+ρ_h t, and the associator is β(k_i,h_i,g_i). Relative versions impose the stated identity and zero boundary conditions.

For every finite ordered simplicial complex and finite data (G,A,ρ,β) in the definition, the displayed operations define a finite 2-groupoid, including every relative version. For x=(a,B), π₂=ker(δ_a:C⁰→C¹); every 2-isomorphism class of raw 1-automorphisms has |im δ_a| elements, so |π₁|=|S_x|/|im δ_a|. The corresponding relative formulas hold. On a single vertex, π₁=G and π₂=A, with associator determined by β.

seams_checked.note: Checked the realization definition and coupling theorem against the supplier definitions and proofs. They preserve the left action, tetrahedron signs, gauge correction, raw arrows, 2-arrow relation and associator. Model-dependent phases remain separate assumptions.

Both examples use the supplier gauge formulas faithfully on the closed boundary of a 4-simplex. Their split and nonzero-Postnikov computations agree with the supplier conventions; unit response is separately adopted model data.

The gauging definition and higher gluing theorem retain raw gauge multiplicities, vertex gauge-of-gauge cochains, relative boundary conditions and the kernel/image stabilizer formulas. The higher measure is |π₂|/|π₁|, including point weight |A|/|G|; the ordinary groupoid theorem is explicitly distinguished.
